what: Byte ranges of mission-save record packets that differ between two saves of the same state although nothing in the state differs. tools/save_inspect.py diff --mask applies it; any differing byte outside it is a real difference.
why: Records are written as raw memory images, so uninitialised bytes, padding and pointers reach the file. A class-level 'noisy record' list hid a regression inside a record; a byte mask does not.
format: classes.<record class>.run = ranges [lo, hi] (inclusive byte offsets inside one record) that differ between two runs of ONE exe; .build = ranges that differ only between DIFFERENT exes (applied with --across-builds). Every class not listed here, and every FIT text packet, is compared byte for byte.
measured: mc2_01 quicksave at render frame 1000, exes 1266aa1a2 (pair f_a/f_c), 06ea51611 (g_a/g_b) and 45f39522a (h_a/h_b), all with the Team::Save fix; `py -3 tools/save_inspect.py ranges A B` over each pair. The MechWarriorData and MechData ranges were identical in all three pairs (gaps under 16 bytes joined). CommanderData differed in different places in each pair (234, 341, 608 bytes), so it is masked from its first to its last noisy byte and is NOT a proof surface; the B1 batches write no commander.
pilot_text_fields: MechWarriorData bytes 1-180 are the pilot strings (name 1-80, callsign 81-100, video 101-120, audio 121-140, brain 141-180); bytes 184-2167 are numeric pilot state (index, paint scheme, rank, skills, kill and skill tables, goals). The whole range 0-2167 was byte-identical in every run pair and across all three exes of the mission-boot saves measured here, and it is deliberately outside the mask. In a campaign save byte 220 (escapesThruEjection, rolled with RandomNumber(100) when a pilot is created) differs between two separate captures; tools/campaign_save_roundtrip.py skips it, a re-save of a loaded save does not differ there.
known_writer_defects: MechWarriorData 2192-2451, 3188-3447 and 3520-3779 (one pilot record, index 9 of 120 in the stock mc2_01 save): 24 four-byte words in the three TacticalOrder blocks (tacOrder, lastTacOrder, curTacOrder, 332 bytes each). They are never initialised by the order code, hold image-relative addresses that change with every link and are equal between two runs of one exe. A pre-existing save-writer defect for the save-format arc: initialise TacticalOrder and write records through a zeroed staging copy.

MechData and GroundVehicleData bytes 2952-2955 and 3000-3003 of every record: the vftable pointers of the embedded MoverControl (2952) and MoverDynamics (3000). Inert on load (mover_misc.cpp copy-assigns). Same defect class.
MechData 3020-3035 (one record): uninitialised bytes that differ between two runs of one exe.

MechWarriorData 10072-14871 and 14920-19719 (4800 bytes each, 48 % of every pilot record): MovePath::stepList[200] of moveOrders.path[0] and path[1] (record offset 7348 + 2684 + 40 and + 4848; 24-byte PathStep, mclib/move.h). Entries past numSteps are never written and the byte after PathStep::direction is padding, so they hold leftovers that differ between two runs of one exe. Same defect class. No B1 batch touches movement orders, so masking them hides no B1 change.

The three 260-byte build ranges of MechWarriorData cover each TacticalOrder block as a whole in all 120 records, although only one record (index 9) was observed to differ (24 words). Unobserved bytes of a block could hide a change inside it; no B1 batch writes orders.
